_comment: Expected MySQL configuration and counter baselines for a deployment, used by
the `check-health` skill (§10) to detect config drift and judge counters.
Copy to deploy/mysql-baseline.json and fill in real values. That file is
gitignored because container names, host paths and tuning values are
deployment-specific — this repo is public. Same pattern as compute-nodes.json.
The AUTHORITATIVE source of these settings is the private infra repo that owns
the MySQL compose stack. This file is a check-against baseline, not a deploy
artifact: nothing reads it to configure MySQL, only to notice when MySQL has
_persisted_config_comment: mysqld-auto.cnf lives in the datadir and is the ONLY home for any setting not
passed on the command line or in an option file. It survives restart, reboot
and container recreation because the datadir is a bind mount — but it is NOT
in any repo, so a lost or rebuilt volume silently reverts every value below to
the MySQL default. That is the failure this baseline exists to catch.

variable_notes.innodb_buffer_pool_size: The one that matters most. If it reads 134217728 (128 MB, the stock default) the config has been lost — expect the verification cache rebuild to go from ~90 s toward ~40 min. Treat as an incident, not a note.
variable_notes.innodb_redo_log_capacity: PERSIST_ONLY — the running value only changes at the next MySQL start. A mismatch between the running value and this baseline is EXPECTED until then, and is not drift.
variable_notes.max_connections: Was briefly lowered and reverted. Lowering it frees no memory at steady state; see the connection-attribution check before touching it.
variable_notes.slow_query_log_file: Must be an explicit stable path. MySQL's default is <hostname>-slow.log, and in Docker the hostname is the container ID — so on any container recreation MySQL silently starts a NEW log file and orphans the old one, muting anything keyed to the filename.

baseline_counters._comment: Lifetime totals from a long-uptime instance. Judge by RATE across a window, never by the lifetime figure — several of these are large purely because of past backfills.

counter_notes.Innodb_buffer_pool_wait_free: Lifetime figure is historical (accumulated during backfills) and measured ZERO across a 21 h window. A large number here is not evidence of a current problem.
counter_notes.Innodb_log_waits: Should stay 0. Non-zero means the redo log is a bottleneck.
counter_notes.Connection_errors_max_connections: Non-zero means the connection ceiling has actually been hit. Attribute it before acting — it is usually not this app.

expected_slow_log_fingerprints._comment: Queries known to appear and already understood. The value of the slow log is what appears that is NOT on this list. Update it when a phase retires one.
known: INSERT INTO verification_daily_stats ... SELECT  (the daily rollup itself)
mysqldump  (nightly backup; identify by SQL_NO_CACHE and exclude)
